description:
The preregistration document that fixes what the campaign estimates, on which cells, at what sample sizes, under what error budget, with what failure and exclusion rules — written and committed before any campaign matrix is drawn.

## Background

The conjecture under study is asymptotic: $\Pr[\mathrm{per}(A) = 0] = 1/q + o(1)$ is a statement about $n \to \infty$, and no finite grid of $n$ can confirm or contradict it in either direction, since an asymptotic statement is compatible with any finite prefix of the sequence. What finite data can address is the finite-$n$ correction $\delta(n) = \Pr[\mathrm{per}(A) = 0] - 1/q$ — its sign, its magnitude, and how it varies with $n$ and $q$ — and the pipeline that measures it.

The proved results bound that quantity far too loosely to substitute for measurement. The floor $\Pr \ge 1/q$ holds for every $n$ at odd characteristic; the ceiling $\Pr \le 1/q + 11/q^3$ holds for $n \ge 3$ but sits $0.03$ to $0.41$ above the floor, between one-and-a-half and three-and-a-half orders of magnitude looser than the deviations a campaign can resolve.

Preregistration is what separates this campaign from the by-product statistics that preceded it. Those cells had no fixed sample size and no stopping rule, and one of them — a $q = 7$, $n = 20$ reading $2.30$ standard errors below the floor — is exactly the shape of result that a post-hoc threshold manufactures. An earlier revision of the feasibility study spent its top recommendation chasing an apparent below-floor signal that proved to be two measurement defects plus fluctuation.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The estimand is stated as $\delta(n) = \Pr[\mathrm{per}(A) = 0] - 1/q$ over the measured range, with the explicit record that no finite grid tests an asymptotic statement in either direction.
- [hard] REQ-02: $N$ per cell is fixed from the measured envelope before any campaign matrix is drawn and is not revised in response to observed values, and no stopping rule is keyed on the observed statistic.
- [hard] REQ-03: The cell universe names a core processor-feasible grid — all $n$ from $4$ to the per-$q$ frontier, the frontier at a standard error of $10^{-3}$ being $n = 28$ at $q = 3$, $n = 24$ at $q = 5$ and $n = 20$ at $q = 7$, giving $K = 63$ cells — together with any predeclared accelerator-contingent extension cells.
- [hard] REQ-04: Extension cells either enter the multiplicity accounting with the core grid or are placed in an explicitly gatekept second family whose entry condition is stated before any draw.
- [hard] REQ-05: A global error budget is allocated numerically across the permanent-floor family and the determinant family, and the per-cell level each family uses follows from that allocation.
- [hard] REQ-06: Acceptance decisions are specified as exact binomial tests — one-sided against the composite null $\Pr \ge 1/q$ evaluated at $p = 1/q$, and two-sided against $1 - \prod_{i=1}^{n}(1 - q^{-i})$ — with normal-approximation critical values recorded as planning approximations only.
- [hard] REQ-07: Exclusion and failure rules are predeclared: what halts a cell, what quarantines a shard, what may be rerun, how many attempts are permitted, and how a rerun charges the error budget.
- [hard] REQ-08: Backend selection is specified as a function of correctness, safety and measured throughput alone, and explicitly never of an observed zero fraction.
- [hard] REQ-09: The $q = 7$, $n = 20$ cell is committed as the first cell resampled under a preregistered $N$, and the by-product reading motivating that choice stays on the record whatever the resample returns.
- [hard] REQ-10: The validation plan names the exact enumeration anchors — $q = 3$ up to $n = 4$, $q = 5$ and $q = 7$ up to $n = 3$ — and requires sampler and estimator agreement with them before any estimated cell is believed.
- [hard] REQ-11: The $q = 3$ arm is framed as reproduction and precision against published numerics, with no wording implying the campaign extends the $q = 3$ curve in $n$.
- [hard] REQ-12: The convergence-shape comparison is preregistered as a likelihood comparison on observed counts under their binomial sampling distribution, with the range of $n$ over which candidate families are distinguishable reported rather than assumed.
- [hard] REQ-13: Novelty statements are conditional on the recorded literature search, naming what was searched, what it returned, and that search's stated limits.
- [hard] REQ-14: The protocol defines a cell's terminal states — completed only with every manifested shard, exactly its preregistered $N$, and final estimates and verdicts; or halted with its reason while the summary preserves every valid manifested shard completed before the halt as pooled raw counts but no final estimates or verdicts — so a cell that is neither is an incomplete campaign rather than a silent omission.

## Notes

The protocol is published at the dataset home rather than in an issue-scoped area, since it must outlive the work that produced it and be readable beside the data it governs.

This document carries forward the campaign-design half of the feasibility study's mandate. The study fixed the attainable envelope and closed with a go recommendation and a campaign design; the design is not a finished artefact until it is stated as a protocol that binds a specific campaign, with its cell universe, sample sizes, error budget and failure rules committed in advance. Delivery of the study itself is credited to the completed study work; this document is the contribution that re-validates its design half against what the campaign will actually run, and revises it where measurement since has moved.
title: Scientific preregistration protocol for the campaign
